Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Verify the complete end-to-end comment lifecycle through the actual UI: posting on a Lesson/Quiz, the Rule Engine's APPROVED/PENDING/REJECTED outcomes and their visibility rules, edit re-evaluation, reply/like, own-comment management, and Admin moderation (view/approve/reject/delete) via the Comment Management dashboard.
Learner posts a clean comment on a Lesson and it is visible immediately to everyone.
column3: 1. Log in as Learner A. 2. Open a Lesson's detail page and scroll to the "Discussion" section. 3. Tap the "Write a comment..." field and enter a normal, on-topic comment (e.g. "Could someone explain the difference between the two tenses used here?"). 4. Tap "Post comment".
column4: The Rule Engine finds no blacklist/regex match; status=APPROVED; the comment appears at the top of the Discussion list immediately for Learner A, and is visible to any other Learner who opens the same Lesson's Discussion section.
column5: Learner A has access to the Lesson.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: A comment containing a phone number or URL is flagged suspicious (PENDING) and hidden from everyone except its author.
column3: 1. As Learner A, in the same Lesson's Discussion section, post a comment containing a phone number or a URL (e.g. "Contact me at 0912345678 for tutoring"). 2. Tap "Post comment".
column4: The regex pattern check matches; status=PENDING; a toast reads "Your comment is awaiting moderation and is only visible to you for now."; the comment still appears in Learner A's own Discussion view but is hidden from the public thread for anyone else who opens the same Lesson.
column5: Learner A has access to the Lesson.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: A comment containing a blacklisted offensive keyword is REJECTED and hidden even from its own author.
column3: 1. As Learner A, post a comment containing a known blacklisted word (per CommentRuleEngineService.BLACKLIST_KEYWORDS). 2. Tap "Post comment".
column4: status=REJECTED; a toast reads "Your comment violates community guidelines."; the comment never appears in the Discussion list again for anyone, including Learner A after reloading the Lesson.
column5: Learner A has access to the Lesson; a known blacklisted keyword is available for the test.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: A different Learner viewing the same Lesson never sees another user's PENDING or REJECTED comments.
column3: 1. Log in as Learner B (a different account). 2. Open the same Lesson used in TC02/TC03 and scroll to its Discussion section.
column4: Learner B's Discussion list shows only APPROVED comments (e.g. TC01's) - the PENDING comment from TC02 and the REJECTED comment from TC03 are both absent, even after a manual refresh.
column5: Comments from TC01-TC03 already posted by Learner A on this Lesson.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Editing a REJECTED comment to remove the offending word flips it back to APPROVED automatically.
column3: 1. As Learner A, locate the REJECTED comment from TC03 in the Discussion list (still visible/editable to its own author even while rejected) and tap its edit (pencil) icon. 2. Edit out the blacklisted word, leaving clean text. 3. Save the edit.
column4: The edit re-runs the same Rule Engine evaluation; with no blacklist/regex match now, status flips to APPROVED and the comment becomes visible in the Discussion list for everyone - there is no separate "resubmit for review" step.
column5: The REJECTED comment from TC03 exists and is still visible to its author.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Editing a previously clean APPROVED comment to insert a blacklisted word gets it re-evaluated to REJECTED.
column3: 1. As Learner A, tap the edit (pencil) icon on the APPROVED comment from TC01. 2. Edit it to insert a blacklisted keyword. 3. Save the edit.
column4: The edit re-runs the Rule Engine on the new text; status changes to REJECTED and the comment disappears from the Discussion list for everyone, including Learner A on reload - confirming a user cannot post clean then sneak in bad content via edit.
column5: The APPROVED comment from TC01 exists.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: A second Learner replies to the first Learner's comment and the original author is notified.
column3: 1. Log in as Learner B. 2. On an APPROVED root comment (e.g. a freshly re-approved TC01 after TC06 is reverted, or a new clean comment), tap "Reply". 3. Enter a clean message in the reply box and tap the reply "Reply" submit action.
column4: The reply nests visually under the root comment in the Discussion thread; assuming the reply is itself APPROVED, Learner A (the root comment's author) receives a CommentReply notification in their Bell (cross-reference SYS_FLOW_NTF_TC03).
column5: An APPROVED root comment from Learner A exists.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Learner likes then unlikes a comment, and the like count updates correctly both ways.
column3: 1. As Learner B, tap the Like icon on an APPROVED comment and note the count shown next to it. 2. Tap the same Like icon again to unlike.
column4: The like count increments by 1 and the icon switches to its "liked" color immediately after liking; both revert to the original state after unliking.

column3: 1. As Learner A, open one of their own APPROVED comments in the Discussion list and tap its Delete (trash) icon. 2. Confirm in the "Delete Comment" dialog ("Are you sure you want to delete this comment? This action cannot be undone.").
column4: The comment is removed from the Discussion list immediately; it no longer appears on reload for any user.
column5: Learner A owns at least one comment on the Lesson.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: A Learner cannot edit or delete another user's comment; forcing the action directly hits a masked 500, not a clean 403.
column3: 1. As Learner B, view a comment authored by Learner A in the Discussion list - confirm no edit (pencil) or delete (trash) icon is rendered for it, since the UI only shows those controls on the viewer's own comments. 2. Force the same edit/delete action directly against Learner A's comment id (bypassing the UI, since it exposes no control for this).
column4: Step 1: no edit/delete affordance is shown for a comment Learner B does not own - the normal UI path is fully blocked. Step 2: the forced action is rejected with a generic 500 Internal Server Error rather than a clean 403/404 (the real "not allowed to edit/delete this comment" error is masked, per itc-sheet-comment.csv COMMENT_FT10) - Learner A's comment remains unchanged either way.
column5: Learner A owns a comment; Learner B is logged in; reaching step 2 requires bypassing the UI directly since it never exposes another user's comment id for editing.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Admin filters the Comment Management queue by Pending status and finds the flagged comment with full context.
column3: 1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR. 2. Open Comment Management. 3. Use the Status filter dropdown and select "Pending".
column4: The PENDING comment from TC02 appears in the table with its Commenter / Comment / Course / Lesson-Quiz / Status / Created columns correctly populated.
column5: The PENDING comment from TC02 exists.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Admin opens Comment Detail and sees the original text, normalized text, detection reason, status, author, and created time.
column3: 1. From the Comment Management table, click the "View Detail" (eye) icon on the PENDING comment from TC02.
column4: The "Comment Detail" dialog shows Original Comment (as typed), Normalized Comment (lowercased/accent-stripped/leetspeak-normalized), Detection Reason (which pattern matched), Current Status, and the commenter's name/email plus Course/Lesson-Quiz/created time in the header.
column5: The PENDING comment from TC02 exists.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Admin approves a PENDING comment from the detail dialog, making it visible to everyone.
column3: 1. From the Comment Detail dialog (TC12), click "Approve".
column4: Status changes to Approved (the dialog's Current Status chip only ever offers Pending/Approved/Rejected - there is no free-text status field anywhere in the UI, even though the API itself accepts an arbitrary string per itc-sheet-comment.csv COMMENT_FT14); the comment now appears in the public Discussion thread for all users, not just the original author.
column5: The PENDING comment from TC02 exists.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Admin deletes a comment (including one it doesn't own) from the table and it is removed for everyone.
column3: 1. From the Comment Management table, click the Delete (trash) icon on any comment (any status/author) and confirm in the "Delete Comment" dialog.
column4: The comment is hard-deleted; it disappears from both the Comment Management table and the public Lesson Discussion thread.

Lesson Comment- Like & Moderation Flow: Posting a comment containing an HTML/script tag payload is checked for whether it renders as executable content.
column3: 1. As a Learner, post a comment whose text is or . 2. If it becomes APPROVED (no blacklist/regex match on this payload), view the Discussion thread as another user.
column4: The Flutter UI's Text widgets render the payload as inert, literal on-screen text (e.g. the visible string "<script>alert('x')</script>") since Flutter never interprets comment content as HTML - no script execution is possible through this client, so this specific UI case should Pass. However, per itc-sheet-comment.csv COMMENT_FT12 the raw content is still stored and returned by the API completely unescaped (documented, not yet fixed at the data layer) - record this as a live data-layer gap relevant to any future non-Flutter consumer of the same API, even though it is not exploitable through today's app.
column5: Learner has access to a Lesson.
